raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

The chunked sparse prefill passes `query_start_loc`, `seq_lens` and `gather_lens` to `CombineTopkSwaIndicesKernel` as views at `num_decodes` and `chunk_start` offsets, so each of these int32 pointers lands on any 4-byte offset. Triton specializes on that alignment, and the three warmed alignment variants miss reachable combinations: every DeepSeek-V4.1 server compiles the kernel 6 more times during serving (2 alignments x 3 compress ratios), and the JIT monitor reports `CombineTopkSwaIndicesKernel` once multi-request prefills arrive.

Each program reads one value from these tensors, so their alignment does not enable vectorized loads. Stop specializing on it (`do_not_specialize`, as #57667 does for `end_ptr`) and warm only the `topk_indices` alignments. This drops the warmup from 3 to 2 variants per compress ratio.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest -q tests/kernels/attention/test_deepseek_v41_combine_topk_swa_warmup.py
pre-commit run --files vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/ops/cache_utils.py \
  tests/kernels/attention/test_deepseek_v41_combine_topk_swa_warmup.py
```

The test warms the kernel, then calls `combine_topk_swa_indices` for compress ratios 0/1/2 with the offset views the chunked prefill passes (`num_decodes = chunk_start = 1`: `query_start_loc` and ROCm's `seq_lens` at offset 2, `gather_lens` at offset 1) under a Triton post-compile hook, and asserts nothing compiles.

MI355X (gfx950), DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP4. Unit test on `main@3966924d56`; kernel time, E2E and GSM8K on `main@5d35ce3934` (each the host build's commit at the time).

## Test Result

Unit test, run from outside the repo with `PYTHONPATH` set to each tree:

| tree | result |
| --- | --- |
| `main@3966924d56` | fails: 3 compiles of `CombineTopkSwaIndicesKernel.kernel` after warmup (one per ratio) |
| this PR without `gather_lens_ptr` in `do_not_specialize` | fails: 3 compiles |
| this PR | passes |

Kernel time (CUDA events, 200 launches; 4 runs per tree in fresh processes, first discarded, median of runs 2-4, within-tree spread < 1%): unchanged where the kernel is GPU-bound (one 16384-token request, compress ratio 1/2: 34.8 us on both), and 7-10% lower (about 2 us) on the launch-bound shapes (512-4096 tokens per request), from the three pointers no longer being alignment-checked at launch.

E2E, AgentX trace replay (1800 s window, concurrency 32), both trees run at the same time on GPUs 0-3 / 4-7 with `--jit-monitor-verbose`:

```bash
vllm serve DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 4 --max-model-len 1048576 \
  --language-model-only --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --moe-backend aiter \
  --max-num-seqs 128 --max-cudagraph-capture-size 1024 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,...}' --jit-monitor-verbose
```

| | main | this PR | delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `CombineTopkSwaIndicesKernel` JIT-monitor reports (4 ranks) | 12 | 0 | |
| total tok/s | 198828 | 199325 | +0.2% |
| output tok/s | 1408.8 | 1411.7 | +0.2% |
| mean TTFT (ms) | 233.9 | 236.4 | +1.1% |
| median TTFT (ms) | 145.6 | 147.1 | +1.0% |
| mean TPOT (ms) | 5.98 | 5.91 | -1.2% |
| median TPOT (ms) | 5.25 | 5.18 | -1.3% |

n=1 per tree; an A/A pair of `main` on the two GPU groups differed by 0.0% total tok/s and 0.5-1.0% in TTFT/TPOT. The other kernels the monitor reports are unchanged and out of scope here.

GSM8K (5-shot, greedy, 1319 questions, `max_gen_toks=256`, prefix caching and speculative decoding off):

| | strict-match | flexible-extract |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| main | 0.9272 | 0.9272 |
| this PR | 0.9272 | 0.9280 |
| main, repeat | 0.9234 | 0.9234 |

Identical prompts on every item; identical generations: main vs this PR 19.9%, main vs main repeat 18.3%. No measurable accuracy change within the base-repeat noise floor.

---

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""CombineTopkSwaIndicesKernel warmup must cover the pointer alignments that the
+chunked sparse prefill passes at runtime."""
+
+import itertools
+from contextlib import contextmanager
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+if not current_platform.is_cuda_alike():
+    pytest.skip("Triton kernels require a GPU", allow_module_level=True)
+
+triton = pytest.importorskip("triton")
+
+from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.common.ops.cache_utils import (  # noqa: E402
+    _COMBINE_TOPK_SWA_INDICES_KERNEL,
+    combine_topk_swa_indices,
+)
+
+TOPK = 512
+WINDOW = 128
+NUM_REQS = 3
+QUERY_LEN = 4
+
+
+def _vllm_config():
+    hf_config = SimpleNamespace(
+        compress_ratios=[0, 0, 2, 2, 1, 1, 0],
+        index_topk=TOPK,
+        sliding_window=WINDOW,
+    )
+    return SimpleNamespace(
+        model_config=SimpleNamespace(hf_config=hf_config),
+        scheduler_config=SimpleNamespace(max_num_batched_tokens=16384),
+    )
+
+
+@contextmanager
+def _record_compiles():
+    from triton import knobs
+
+    previous = knobs.runtime.jit_post_compile_hook
+    compiled: list[str] = []
+
+    def hook(**kwargs):
+        compiled.append(getattr(kwargs.get("fn"), "name", "<unknown>"))
+        if previous is not None:
+            return previous(**kwargs)
+        return None
+
+    knobs.runtime.jit_post_compile_hook = hook
+    try:
+        yield compiled
+    finally:
+        knobs.runtime.jit_post_compile_hook = previous
+
+
+def _int32(values: int, fill: int, offset: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+    buffer = torch.full((offset + values,), fill, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    return buffer[offset:]
+
+
+def test_warmup_covers_chunked_prefill_pointer_alignments():
+    _COMBINE_TOPK_SWA_INDICES_KERNEL.warmup(_vllm_config())
+
+    topk_indices = torch.zeros(
+        (NUM_REQS * QUERY_LEN, TOPK), dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"
+    )
+    with _record_compiles() as compiled:
+        # The chunked prefill passes query_start_loc[num_decodes + chunk_start:]
+        # and gather_lens[chunk_start:]. seq_lens is sliced at num_decodes too
+        # on ROCm, or comes from a fresh buffer, so the int32 pointers land on
+        # every 4-byte offset.
+        for num_decodes, chunk_start, seq_lens_at_num_decodes in itertools.product(
+            range(4), range(4), (True, False)
+        ):

nodes.body:
@frida-andersson Reduced the test to one offset case per compress ratio (`num_decodes = chunk_start = 1`); it still fails on `main` (one runtime compile per ratio) and passes here.

On the comment: `rocm.py` slices `seq_lens` at `chunk_start` only, but the tensor it slices is already `seq_lens[num_decodes:]` (`sparse_swa.py`: `result["prefill_seq_lens"] = seq_lens[num_decodes:]`), so on ROCm its pointer carries the `num_decodes + chunk_start` offset like `query_start_loc`, while `gather_lens` is a fresh buffer and carries `chunk_start` only. I updated the comment to say that.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""CombineTopkSwaIndicesKernel warmup must cover the pointer alignments that the
+chunked sparse prefill passes at runtime."""
+
+from contextlib import contextmanager
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+if not current_platform.is_cuda_alike():
+    pytest.skip("Triton kernels require a GPU", allow_module_level=True)
+
+triton = pytest.importorskip("triton")
+
+from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.common.ops.cache_utils import (  # noqa: E402
+    _COMBINE_TOPK_SWA_INDICES_KERNEL,
+    combine_topk_swa_indices,
+)
+
+TOPK = 512
+WINDOW = 128
+NUM_REQS = 3
+QUERY_LEN = 4
+
+
+def _vllm_config():
+    hf_config = SimpleNamespace(
+        compress_ratios=[0, 0, 2, 2, 1, 1, 0],
+        index_topk=TOPK,
+        sliding_window=WINDOW,
+    )
+    return SimpleNamespace(
+        model_config=SimpleNamespace(hf_config=hf_config),
+        scheduler_config=SimpleNamespace(max_num_batched_tokens=16384),
+    )
+
+
+@contextmanager
+def _record_compiles():
+    from triton import knobs
+
+    previous = knobs.runtime.jit_post_compile_hook
+    compiled: list[str] = []
+
+    def hook(**kwargs):
+        compiled.append(getattr(kwargs.get("fn"), "name", "<unknown>"))
+        if previous is not None:
+            return previous(**kwargs)
+        return None
+
+    knobs.runtime.jit_post_compile_hook = hook
+    try:
+        yield compiled
+    finally:
+        knobs.runtime.jit_post_compile_hook = previous
+
+
+def _int32(values: int, fill: int, offset: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+    buffer = torch.full((offset + values,), fill, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    return buffer[offset:]
+
+
+def test_warmup_covers_chunked_prefill_pointer_alignments():
+    _COMBINE_TOPK_SWA_INDICES_KERNEL.warmup(_vllm_config())
+
+    topk_indices = torch.zeros(
+        (NUM_REQS * QUERY_LEN, TOPK), dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"
+    )
+    # The chunked prefill slices query_start_loc at num_decodes + chunk_start
+    # and gather_lens at chunk_start. ROCm's seq_lens is seq_lens[num_decodes:]
+    # sliced again at chunk_start, so it carries the num_decodes offset too.
+    num_decodes, chunk_start = 1, 1
+    batch_offset = num_decodes + chunk_start
+    query_start_loc = torch.arange(
+        0,
+        (batch_offset + NUM_REQS + 1) * QUERY_LEN,
+        QUERY_LEN,
+        dtype=torch.int32,
+        device="cuda",
+    )[batch_offset : batch_offset + NUM_REQS + 1]
+    seq_lens = _int32(NUM_REQS, 4096, batch_offset)
+    gather_lens = _int32(NUM_REQS, 1024, chunk_start)
+    with _record_compiles() as compiled:
+        for ratio in (0, 1, 2):
+            combine_topk_swa_indices(
+                topk_indices,
+                query_start_loc,
+                seq_lens,
+                gather_lens,
+                WINDOW,
+                ratio,
+                TOPK if ratio else 0,
+                4096,
+                4096,
+            )
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+
+    assert not compiled, f"JIT compiled after warmup: {compiled}"
